study_material.title: Time, Speed and Distance - Complete Study Notes
study_material.introduction: Distance = Speed x Time is the whole chapter; trains, boats and races are just costumes. Master unit conversion (km/h to m/s), relative speed, and the harmonic-mean average speed, and every variant falls quickly.
learning_objectives: Convert km/h to m/s and back instantly
Solve train problems (crossing poles, platforms, other trains)
Use relative speed for same/opposite direction motion

concepts.heading: 1. The Master Formula
concepts.body: D = S x T. Keep units consistent: km/h to m/s multiply by 5/18; m/s to km/h multiply by 18/5. 72 km/h = 20 m/s. If speed ratio is a:b over the same distance, time ratio is b:a.

concepts.heading: 2. Trains
concepts.body: A train crossing a pole covers its own length; crossing a platform or bridge covers train length + platform length. Crossing another train: total distance = sum of lengths, at relative speed (difference if same direction, sum if opposite).

concepts.heading: 3. Relative Speed
concepts.body: Opposite directions: speeds add. Same direction: speeds subtract. Catch-up time = initial gap / relative speed. A thief with a 20 km head start against a 10 km/h faster pursuer is caught in 2 hours.

concepts.heading: 4. Boats and Streams
concepts.body: Downstream speed = boat + stream; upstream = boat - stream. Boat speed = (down + up)/2, stream speed = (down - up)/2. Given distances and times each way, compute the two speeds first.

concepts.heading: 5. Average Speed
concepts.body: Average speed = total distance / total time. For equal distances at speeds a and b it is 2ab/(a+b) - never the arithmetic mean. The average always sits closer to the slower speed.

formulas: D = S x T; km/h x 5/18 = m/s
shortcut_methods: Speed ratio a:b means time ratio b:a over equal distance
Trains: always ask 'what total distance must be covered, and at what relative speed?'
common_mistakes: Averaging speeds arithmetically over equal distances
Forgetting the platform length in crossing problems
Using the wrong relative speed direction
Mixing m/s and km/h in one equation
study_material.summary: Fix units, identify the true distance to cover, choose the right (relative) speed, and apply D = ST.
quick_revision_notes: Crossing = sum of lengths at relative speed
Boat = mean of down and up speeds

solved_examples.question: A 150 m train travelling at 54 km/h passes a pole in:
solved_examples.shortcut: Only the train's own length matters for a pole.

solved_examples.question: A 200 m train crosses a 300 m platform in 25 seconds. Its speed is:
solved_examples.step_by_step: Distance = 500 m in 25 s = 20 m/s = 72 km/h.

solved_examples.question: A boat goes 20 km downstream in 2 hours and 12 km upstream in 3 hours. Find the boat's speed in still water.
solved_examples.step_by_step: Down = 10 km/h, Up = 4 km/h. Boat = (10+4)/2 = 7 km/h.

solved_examples.question: Two trains of lengths 150 m and 250 m run towards each other at 60 km/h and 40 km/h. Time to cross each other:
solved_examples.step_by_step: Relative speed = 100 km/h = 250/9 m/s. Distance = 400 m. Time = 400 x 9/250 = 14.4 s.

practice_questions.question: A car covers 90 km in 1.5 hours. Its speed is:
A 120 m train moving at 15 m/s passes a signal pole in:
Walking at 4 km/h for 45 minutes covers:
A car travels a distance at 40 km/h and returns at 60 km/h. Average speed for the round trip:
A 240 m train at 30 m/s crosses a 360 m bridge in:
Two runners' speeds are in ratio 3:4. Over the same distance, their times are in ratio:
practice_questions.explanation: Time is inversely proportional to speed.

practice_questions.question: A boat travels downstream at 12 km/h and upstream at 8 km/h. The stream's speed is:
Two trains with total length 300 m run in opposite directions at 54 km/h and 36 km/h. They cross each other in:
A thief drives at 40 km/h with a 30-minute head start. Police pursue at 50 km/h. Time to catch the thief:
practice_questions.explanation: Head start gap = 20 km; relative speed 10 km/h: 20/10 = 2 hours.

questions.question: A bus covers 300 km in 5 hours. Its average speed is:
A 180 m train at 20 m/s passes a pole in:
A man walking at 5 km/h crosses a 1.25 km bridge in:
A 150 m train crosses a 250 m platform in 20 s. Its speed is:
Two trains of lengths 100 m and 150 m run in the same direction at 60 km/h and 40 km/h. The faster train passes the slower in:
questions.explanation: Relative speed 20 km/h = 50/9 m/s; 250 x 9/50 = 45 s.

questions.question: A boat's still-water speed is 15 km/h in a 3 km/h stream. Time to go 30 km downstream:
questions.explanation: Downstream 18 km/h; 30/18 h = 5/3 h = 1 h 40 min.

questions.question: A car goes out at 30 km/h and returns over the same road at 60 km/h. Average speed:
Walking at 3/4 of his usual speed, a man is 10 minutes late to office. His usual time is:
questions.explanation: At 3/4 speed, time becomes 4/3 of usual; the extra 1/3 of usual time = 10 min, so usual = 30 min.

questions.question: A train overtakes a man walking at 6 km/h (same direction) in 18 seconds. The train is 150 m long. The train's speed is:
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 150/18 m/s = 25/3 m/s = 30 km/h. Train = 30 + 6 = 36 km/h.
